column3: “As the green vegetation I have given you everything” preserves one giving clause, rather than separate past and present giving clauses.
“Its life, its blood” preserves the apposition compressed into “lifeblood.”
The demand concerns human blood and life, sought “from the hand” of animals and humans; it does not explicitly say that the animal’s own life is required. “I will require” recurs three times.
“In the image of God He made man” names God within the image phrase rather than saying “in His own image.”
“Swarm on the earth” preserves the teeming image rendered “spread out.”
“Your seed” preserves the collective image rendered “your descendants.”
The verse ends with the further phrase “to every beast of the earth.”
“All flesh” preserves the body image rendered “all life.”
“My bow” preserves the bow image rendered specifically “My rainbow.”
“Every living creature in all flesh” preserves the body expression rendered “of every kind”; the same “all flesh” recurs for what the flood destroys.
“The bow will be in the cloud” preserves a statement of presence rather than “whenever the rainbow appears.” “All flesh” preserves the expression rendered “of every kind.”
“All flesh” preserves the collective body expression rendered “every creature.”
“To them” retains the pronominal recipient instead of explicitly naming “Shem.”
“May God make room for Japheth” does not explicitly add “the territory”; the final recipient remains pronominal, “to them.”
